headline: HSC exams: Special chance for students who missed tests due to weather
summary: Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haq Miloon announced that students who missed exams due to adverse weather will be allowed to retake them.
details: Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haq Miloon informed the National Parliament on Wednesday that students who missed their HSC and equivalent exams due to adverse weather will be given a special opportunity to retake them.
These students will be allowed to take the exams using the same question papers as the postponed exams of the Chittagong Education Board.
The Minister stated that since the HSC examination is a critical stage in a student's life, this special consideration was provided to ensure no one is disadvantaged.
Additionally, the Minister announced that full marks will be awarded for two incorrect questions in the Physics First Paper, where errors in the question paper were identified.
Those responsible for the drafting of the incorrect Physics questions have already been temporarily suspended from their duties.

A total of 12.7 lakh students participated in the HSC exams across the country. Exams were postponed in five districts under the Chittagong Board: Chittagong, Cox's Bazar, Khagrachari, Rangamati, and Bandarban due to heavy rain and adverse weather.

Students from other districts, including Dhaka, who missed exams due to various unavoidable reasons or weather, can also participate in the exams on the same date as the Chittagong Board's postponed tests.
caption:
Missed your HSC exam due to bad weather? You can now retake it.

Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haq Miloon informed the National Parliament on Wednesday that students who missed their HSC and equivalent exams due to adverse weather will be given a special opportunity to retake them.

These students will be allowed to take the exams using the same question papers as the postponed exams of the Chittagong Education Board.

The Minister stated that since the HSC examination is a critical stage in a student's life, this special consideration was provided to ensure no one is disadvantaged.

Additionally, the Minister announced that full marks will be awarded for two incorrect questions in the Physics First Paper, where errors in the question paper were identified.

Those responsible for the drafting of the incorrect Physics questions have already been temporarily suspended from their duties.

A total of 12.7 lakh students participated in the HSC exams across the country. Exams were postponed in five districts under the Chittagong Board: Chittagong, Cox's Bazar, Khagrachari, Rangamati, and Bandarban due to heavy rain and adverse weather.

Students from other districts, including Dhaka, who missed exams due to various unavoidable reasons or weather, can also participate in the exams on the same date as the Chittagong Board's postponed tests.

headline_marked: Bangladesh enacts [[new anti-trafficking law to curb tech-enabled crimes]]
headline: Bangladesh enacts new anti-trafficking law to curb tech-enabled crimes
summary: The Human Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling Prevention and Suppression Act, 2026 aims to dismantle organised criminal networks using digital platforms.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced the Human Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling Prevention and Suppression Act, 2026, designed to strengthen the fight against organised crime.
The new law specifically targets criminal networks that use digital platforms and technology to facilitate trafficking and smuggling, bringing legal capacity up to international standards.
Speaking at a national dissemination programme in Dhaka, the minister described the legislation as a milestone in combating serious transnational crimes.
The law now clearly defines human trafficking and migrant smuggling as separate offences and establishes a comprehensive framework for investigation and prosecution.
Key provisions include expanded protections for victims and witnesses, strengthened trial powers, and increased scope for international cooperation.
A central principle of the act is the non-punishment of victims, ensuring their dignity, rights, and safety are protected throughout the criminal justice process.
The event was jointly organised by the Home Ministry and Justice and Care Bangladesh, attended by high-level officials and international diplomats.
caption:
Bangladesh is upgrading its legal arsenal to fight human trafficking. A new law now targets tech-enabled crimes and organised networks.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced the Human Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling Prevention and Suppression Act, 2026, designed to strengthen the fight against organised crime.

The new law specifically targets criminal networks that use digital platforms and technology to facilitate trafficking and smuggling, bringing legal capacity up to international standards.

Speaking at a national dissemination programme in Dhaka, the minister described the legislation as a milestone in combating serious transnational crimes.

The law now clearly defines human trafficking and migrant smuggling as separate offences and establishes a comprehensive framework for investigation and prosecution.

Key provisions include expanded protections for victims and witnesses, strengthened trial powers, and increased scope for international cooperation.

A central principle of the act is the non-punishment of victims, ensuring their dignity, rights, and safety are protected throughout the criminal justice process.

The event was jointly organised by the Home Ministry and Justice and Care Bangladesh, attended by high-level officials and international diplomats.
